articles.title: Identifying household water shutoff locations
articles.summary: Plan how to find the water isolation controls without attempting unsafe building work.

sections.title: Identify responsible controls
paragraphs: A flat or house may have a main water stop tap, separate appliance controls or building-managed isolation points. Their location and responsibility vary, especially in shared properties.
Ask the landlord, managing agent or water supplier which controls residents are permitted to operate. Do not interfere with unknown communal pipework or inaccessible service areas.

sections.title: Create an offline record
paragraphs: Record an accurate description of approved controls in the private household plan and clarify which one serves your own home.
A simple labelled photo can aid recognition, but avoid publicly posting access details for secure building service rooms or equipment.

sections.title: Review before an incident
paragraphs: If a control appears damaged, seized or unclear, request qualified plumbing help instead of forcing it. Do not assume that turning any nearby valve will isolate a leak.
Keep the plumber and building-management contacts available when the internet is unavailable.

articles.title: Window and door draught inspection
articles.summary: Spot drafts and maintenance gaps while respecting fire exits and building ventilation.

sections.title: Locate comfort problems
paragraphs: Note areas where a window or external door appears to admit unwanted air. Record whether the concern is recurring, seasonal or associated with visible damage.
Do not obstruct required ventilation, fire doors, escape routes or manufacturer-specified air openings; some buildings rely on these for safe operation.

sections.title: Plan appropriate work
paragraphs: Consult the landlord or appropriate tradesperson when adjustments could affect safety, glazing, accessibility or communal elements. Choose compatible products only after checking the door or window instructions.
Temporary fixes must not interfere with locks, closing mechanisms, smoke seals or accessibility. This guide does not provide a universal sealing method.

sections.title: Track follow-up
paragraphs: Record the room, symptom and person responsible for maintenance. Review whether the issue was resolved after appropriate work.
For rented or shared accommodation, responsibilities and permission requirements may differ from owner-occupied homes.

articles.title: Safe storage of household cleaning products
articles.summary: Reduce accidental chemical exposure through organised storage and readable labels.

sections.title: Understand product labels
paragraphs: Cleaning chemicals have different warnings, storage conditions and compatibility rules. Keep products in their original labelled containers wherever possible.
Never infer that household products are compatible because they are used in the same room. The manufacturer label and relevant safety instructions are the primary reference.

sections.title: Separate and restrict access
paragraphs: Choose storage appropriate to the products and away from children or pets when necessary. Keep packaging intact and avoid transferring a chemical into an unlabelled drinking container.
Do not mix substances or experiment with reactions to create homemade cleaners; hazardous fumes or splashes may result.

sections.title: Review the cupboard
paragraphs: Periodically remove leaking or damaged containers using manufacturer and local waste guidance. Keep an inventory of product names only if useful for replacement planning.
The article is an informational storage draft, not a chemical-handling procedure, and any detailed hazardous steps need qualified review.
